name: Jimbo the Terrible
caption: Lost the held record's only surviving 1996 WLW broadcast to Tidalwave by an illegal-weapon finish.
notes: Managed by "Money Bags" Mike Watson, not separately minted this pass.

name: Tidalwave
caption: One half of the tag team Wave of Destruction; won the held record's only surviving 1996 broadcast over Jimbo the Terrible with help from his manager Poseidon.
notes: Managed by Poseidon, his Wave of Destruction tag partner, not separately minted this pass.

name: Raekwon
caption: “The Master of Destruction,” shown mid-match against Ben Hayes as Night of the Hunted's own surviving Part 1 text breaks off, result unrecorded.
notes: Also a Best Gimmick and Most Hated Wrestler nominee at the Achievement Awards two weeks later.

name: “No Remorse” Ben Hayes
caption: Shown mid-match against Raekwon as Night of the Hunted's own surviving Part 1 text breaks off, result unrecorded.
notes: Managed by Corley Ripburger, who states Hayes previously “won his first match” and “left the WLW” under a different management, not separately minted this pass.

name: Gigantor
caption: Billed for Night of the Hunted's own main event against Samhain, hyped on commentary as a show-stopping attraction whose result does not survive.
notes: Also a Most Hated Wrestler nominee at the Achievement Awards two weeks later.

identity.note: Shares a ring name with records of other promotions; no roster, billing or chronology links them.

name: Samhain
caption: The reigning WLW World Heavyweight Champion, billed for Night of the Hunted's own main event against Gigantor, and voted the Achievement Awards' Best Gimmick two weeks later.
notes: The corpus does not narrate how or when he won the World Heavyweight Championship; already champion by 28 Apr 1996. Also a Most Hated Wrestler and Best Trash Talker nominee at the same awards.

name: “Top Dog” Rick Styles

tenures.source: Billed challenger across the Nov-Dec cards, earning his World Title shot by defeating The Gangsta at Holiday Bash and challenging for the title 29 Dec 1996.

The fed's own relaunch manifesto names him the reigning Ultimate Champion as of 15 Mar 1997, having dethroned "Offensive" Alex Adams (msg_id cth9FV2ortYJ); a third-party résumé quoted inside the fed's own Summer Dreams '97 broadcast reads "2 Time UEW Ultimate champion and Dog lover" (msg_id uyYgcU9iDRUJ, 16 Jul 1997).
tenures.note: Billed a three-time UEW Ultimate Champion across 1997 per the fed's own cards; exact dates for the second and third reigns are not recovered.

tenures.source: Billed for the second night on the event's own lineup of 2 June 2002; the event was called off before it was held.

caption: Billed for Night of the Hunted's own crowning of the first WLW North American Champion against Banger, though the surviving text breaks off before the result, and voted the Achievement Awards' Best Trash Talker two weeks later.
notes: Also a Best Gimmick and Most Hated Wrestler nominee at the same awards.

identity.note: Name collision only: a same-named character in another wing (rick-styles-upw); no shared operator, chronology or storyline evidence in the DWO's own documents.

A fragment of the name only: Rick, a backstage figure of the FAW in 2001; Rick, half of a commentary team; and Styles, a one-match wrestler of 2004. None is billed Rick Styles, and no fed, year or document ties any of them to "Top Dog" Rick Styles.
Shares its billed name with wrestlers held in other promotions; no roster, operator or document ties this supercard billing to any of them.

name: Banger
caption: Billed as Rick Styles' opponent for the crowning of the first WLW North American Champion at Night of the Hunted.
notes: Possibly the same wrestler billed “Johnny Banger” among the Achievement Awards' Most Popular Wrestler nominees two weeks later; not confidently resolved by this pass.

name: Spartan
caption: Voted the Achievement Awards' Most Popular Wrestler.

name: “The Fantasy” Bret Young
caption: Voted the Achievement Awards' Most Hated Wrestler for attacking his own cousin; also a Best Gimmick and Best Trash Talker nominee at the same awards.

name: Grave Digga
caption: Voted the Achievement Awards' Best Newcomer.

name: Randy Ventura
caption: WLW President, who opened Night of the Hunted from the ring and introduced Alanis Morissette's own anthem performance.

name: Mike Baldwin
caption: One of the WLW's own broadcast team, calling both Night of the Hunted and co-hosting the Achievement Awards, corroborating the promotion's three-person commentary team.

name: “Big J” Johnny Townsand
caption: One of the WLW's own broadcast team, calling both Night of the Hunted and co-hosting the Achievement Awards, corroborating the promotion's three-person commentary team.

name: Tom Russel
caption: The third of the WLW's own three-person broadcast team, co-hosting the Achievement Awards alongside Mike Baldwin and Johnny Townsand.
